headline: PAGASA Raises Red Rainfall Warning Across Metro Manila and Parts of Luzon
seoTitle: PAGASA Raises Red Rainfall Warning Across Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Metro Manila, Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan and specified parts of Tarlac, Batangas, Cavite and Rizal under a Red warning on August 29.
keywords: Habagat Red warning Metro Manila Luzon
deck: The 11 a.m. warning placed Metro Manila and broad areas of Central Luzon under the highest rainfall-warning level as the Habagat continued to affect Luzon and the Visayas.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA placed Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila and specified areas of Tarlac, Batangas, Cavite and Rizal under a Red rainfall warning at 11 a.m. Saturday, August 29. Serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas covered by the highest warning level.
Orange and Yellow warnings covered other specified areas of Central and Southern Luzon. PAGASA said flooding was threatening in Orange-warning areas and possible in Yellow-warning areas.

sections.heading: Weather systems
paragraphs: PAGASA's 4 a.m. national forecast located an LPA about 520 kilometers north-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes at 3 a.m. and identified the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat as affecting Luzon and the Visayas.

The forecast attributed monsoon rains over Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac and Pampanga to the Habagat. It did not say the LPA had become a tropical cyclone or establish that the LPA itself caused the short-fuse rainfall warning.

sections.heading: Habagat remains a concern
paragraphs: PAGASA forecast possible flash floods or landslides from heavy to intense monsoon rains in the most affected provinces. Moderate to strong southwesterly winds were also expected over Luzon, with moderate to rough coastal waters of 1.5 to 3.1 meters.
Rainfall-warning boundaries can change within hours. Residents should use the latest regional warning for immediate decisions rather than relying on an earlier province list.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: This is an update to the established FMB News weather route. The morning bulletin repeated the developing-LPA and Habagat story but included unsupported class-suspension, emergency-center and rainfall-accumulation details, which are not carried here.
The new official warning materially expands the documented Red-warning area beyond the prior Central Luzon coverage, including Metro Manila and specified parts of Southern Luzon.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rain can quickly worsen flooding and slope instability. Communities near rivers, drainage channels and steep terrain should follow evacuation, road-closure and safety instructions from local disaster authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should follow the latest PAGASA rainfall warnings, local disaster advisories and any subsequent tropical cyclone bulletins if the monitored LPA develops further.
